_comment: End-to-end CLI latency budgets: shell to prompt, including Node startup. Distinct from budgets.json, which bounds walker throughput and memory. These are ceilings on what a person waits for, set roughly 35% above the measured median on the reference machine so ordinary scheduling noise does not fail a build while a real regression still does.
_reference: Apple Silicon laptop, local SSD, Node 26. Recalibrate with --json on the target hardware before enforcing in CI.

version.description: Process start and module graph only. Answered before Commander is built, so this rises the moment anything is added to the entry point's static imports.

tiny-100.description: The common interactive case: select, load, format, write.

tiny-100-tree.description: Selection and tree rendering, no file contents.

tiny-100-dry.description: Selection only. The floor for anything that walks the tree.

_measured: Clean medians on the reference machine at the time of writing: version 34, empty 82, tiny-100 97, display 95, only-tree 83, dry-run 81 ms. Budgets sit ~35% above these.
_noise: Check the reported mad (median absolute deviation) before believing a delta. On an idle machine it is ~1-2 ms; a mad above ~5 ms means something else was running and the medians are not comparable. On a machine that will not go quiet, use latency-ab.bench.js instead — it compares two checkouts in interleaved pairs, so shared load cancels out.
